subject.title: fix(sessions): enforce exact owner equality for all parent session use and narrow catch

question: Should plugin-runtime session mutations fail closed on every existing ownerless session row, including parent use and explicit-target takeover, with no migration or compatibility window?
rationale: Exact equality closes the cross-plugin access path, but ownerless rows may exist from older releases and rejecting them can intentionally stop previously working plugin workflows; repository policy treats that upgrade/security tradeoff as maintainer-owned.

options.title: Approve fail-closed ownership
options.body: Treat ownerless rows as having no plugin authority, coordinate the create and patch PRs around one shared guard, and document the intentional upgrade boundary in merge context.

options.title: Add an explicit migration
options.body: Define a trusted doctor or operator-owned migration that assigns or retires legacy ownerless rows before enforcing exact ownership at runtime.

options.title: Preserve ownerless compatibility
options.body: Allow a narrowly specified legacy behavior temporarily, with tests, a security rationale, and a dated removal plan.

recommendation.title: Approve fail-closed ownership
recommendation.body: Treat ownerless rows as having no plugin authority, coordinate the create and patch PRs around one shared guard, and document the intentional upgrade boundary in merge context.

likelyOwner.reason: The existing review discussion already identified this person for the ownerless-session security and compatibility decision.
